title: Unit and counit for the rational projective line
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$, and let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, in the geometric standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the continuous-function condensed ring $\underline E$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring $\underline{\Qlb}$ of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to each scheme as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module objects over the pulled-back coefficient sheaves, with derived pullback and direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], and Tate twists [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. Here $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of bounded complexes whose cohomology admits a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes with finite constant local models: on a pro-etale cover of each stratum a cohomology module is $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}V$ for a finitely presented scalar module $V$, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $\Loc(\Dbc)$ is the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory containing $\Dbc$ and closed under all small ambient coproducts, using the localizing-closure operation of [sk-def-localizing-closure] for these fixed coefficient sheaves.

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, $q:P=\mathbf P^1_Y=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};Y)\to Y$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_YP$ with
projections $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ and diagonal $\Delta:P\to W$, and let
$\delta_\Lambda:\Delta_*\Lambda_P\to\Lambda_W(1)[2]$ and
$\operatorname{Tr}_q:Rq_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]\to\Lambda_Y$ be the morphisms of
[det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace] and [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients]. All functors below are the restrictions to the
categories $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\Lambda))$.

1. For $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(P,\Lambda))$ there is a natural isomorphism
   $\Delta_*M\simeq p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P$.
2. The *unit* $\eta_M:M\to q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$ is the composite
   $$
   M=Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M\simeq Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P)
   \xrightarrow{Rp_{2*}(1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)}Rp_{2*}\bigl(p_1^*M(1)[2]\bigr)
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }q^*Rq_*M(1)[2],
   $$
   the last arrow being the inverse of the proper base change isomorphism
   $q^*Rq_*\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*$ for the cartesian square formed by $p_1,p_2,q,q$.
3. The *counit* $\varepsilon_K:Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\to K$ for
   $K\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$ is the composite of the projection formula
   isomorphism $Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]$
   with $1\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q$.

Both are natural transformations of exact functors on these localizing
categories.

proof.text: Properness and Noetherianity. By [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], $q$ is proper, and so are $p_1,p_2$, since each is the projective-line projection over $P$ (with the factors interchanged for $p_1$). By [def-weil-proper-morphism] they are separated and of finite type; thus the diagonal $\Delta$ of $q$ is closed. Clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] makes $\Delta$ proper. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] successively to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $q$ and $p_1$: $Y,P,W$ are Noetherian, hence locally Noetherian and quasi-compact.

source.place: Well-definedness (1): proper projections, closed diagonal; existing geometric tools

proof.text: Quasi-separatedness and the open complement. The existing Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] applies to each of the locally Noetherian schemes $Y,P,W$ from Step 1. Together with their quasi-compactness it proves they are qcqs. Put $j:W\setminus\Delta(P)\hookrightarrow W$. For any affine open $V\subseteq W$, the open subscheme $V\setminus\Delta(P)$ of the Noetherian scheme $W$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. This subscheme is $j^{-1}(V)$. Therefore $j$ is a quasi-compact morphism by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. These cited leaves supply the topological subclaims formerly proved inline, including the exact hypothesis required for open--closed exactness.

source.place: Well-definedness (1): qcqs and quasi-compact complement; Stacks 01OY and 01OW/01OZ/0052/04ZA through the existing leaves

proof.text: Standing geometric setting. The structure map $a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type by hypothesis. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] applied to $q,a_Y$, and then to $p_1,a_Yq$, makes $a_P=a_Yq$ and $a_W=a_Yqp_1$ separated and locally of finite type. Both maps are quasi-compact: the only opens of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are empty and the whole space, and their inverse images are empty or the quasi-compact schemes $P,W$ from Step 1. Thus both maps are of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Consequently $Y,P,W$ satisfy the separated-finite-type standing hypothesis in the later rational theorems; all displayed arrows are $k$-morphisms by the fibre-product construction. This argument does not require $Y$ proper over $k$.

source.place: Well-definedness (1)--(3): standing hypotheses; Stacks 01KU and 01T3 composition clauses

proof.text: Coefficient convention. The integer $\ell$ is a unit on $Y,P,W$ and the open complement: its image is nonzero in the field $k$ of characteristic $p\ne\ell$, and structural ring maps carry units to units. This verifies the Tate-twist invertibility hypothesis. The fixed $E$ is a finite subextension of $\Qlb$, whose coefficient ring uses the finite-subextension-valued convention in the statement. The Cartesian-coefficient theorem [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies inverse images of these pulled-back condensed coefficient sheaves, and their Tate twists, with the corresponding coefficient sheaves. It also states that module pullback is exact inverse image. These are the coefficients used throughout the construction.

source.place: Well-definedness (1)--(3): Cartesian condensed coefficient system and twist hypotheses

proof.text: Domains of the functors. The category $\Dbc$ in this statement uses the finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on each stratum its cohomology is locally obtained from a finitely presented scalar module by extension to the coefficient sheaf, and cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval. For these constant-model categories, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] identifies $\Dctf$ with $\Dbc$ and their localizing closures. Its qcqs hypothesis holds for $Y,P,W$ by Steps 1--4. Thus these are precisely the categories $\Loc(\Dctf)$ used in the enclosing unit. Pullbacks preserve these closures and are exact by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback]. Proper pushforwards preserve them and are exact by [det-proper-image-localizing-proper], including $Rq_*,Rp_{i*},R\Delta_*$. Closure under derived tensor is [det-thm-sf-pf-field-tensor]. The coefficient sheaf is a rank-one free module, and the Tate sheaf is locally free of rank one by [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], so each has the finite constant local model with scalar module $\Lambda(*)$ on a single stratum in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: on a trivializing cover the model is $\Lambda_U\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}\Lambda(*)\simeq\Lambda_U$. The scalar module $\Lambda(*)$ is free of rank one over itself, hence finitely presented. Concentrated in degree zero, they therefore belong to $\Dbc$. Consequently tensoring by the Tate sheaf and shifting also preserve these closures. This checks the domain of each object in all three displayed constructions, including unbounded objects in the localizing closure.

source.place: Well-definedness (1)--(3): restriction to the localizing categories

proof.text: Open and closed restrictions detect isomorphisms even on unbounded complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with $X=W$, $i=\Delta$ and ring sheaf $\Lambda_W$. It supplies exact $\Delta_*,j_!$, the identities $\Delta^*\Delta_*\simeq1$, $j^*\Delta_*=0$, and the module sequence $0\to j_!j^*F\to F\to\Delta_*\Delta^*F\to0$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] the two inverse images are exact too. Thus they act on cohomology sheaves. If $\Delta^*C=j^*C=0$ for an arbitrary complex $C$, then the exact sequence applied to each $H^nC$ has zero outer terms, hence $H^nC=0$ for every integer $n$. Applying this observation to the cone of a morphism proves joint conservativity. Exact sheaf functors induce triangulated functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] also identifies the exact closed pushforward with $R\Delta_*$. No assertion about geometric stalks detecting all pro-etale sheaves is needed.

Diagonal tensor identification, with its actual map. Put $A_M=p_1^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Delta_*\Lambda_P$. The tensor-pullback isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the pullback composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and the identities $p_1\Delta=1$ and $\Delta^*\Delta_*\Lambda_P=\Lambda_P$, identify $\Delta^*A_M$ with $M\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_P=M$. The same tensor-pullback isomorphism gives $j^*A_M=0$ because $j^*\Delta_*\Lambda_P=0$. Use the derived pullback/direct-image adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] to form its unit $a_M:A_M\to\Delta_*\Delta^*A_M=\Delta_*M$. After $\Delta^*$ it is an isomorphism: the triangle identity composes it with the invertible closed counit to give $1$. After $j^*$ it is the map $0\to0$. The identities and closed counit here are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], termwise on complexes as in the preceding step. Joint conservativity from Step 6 makes $a_M$ an isomorphism. Define the isomorphism in clause (1) to be $a_M^{-1}$. It is natural in $M$, since $a$ is an adjunction unit followed by natural tensor and pullback identifications.

source.place: Well-definedness (1): construction and invertibility of the diagonal tensor map

proof.text: The initial identification in the unit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $P\xrightarrow{\Delta}W\xrightarrow{p_2}P$, with the pulled-back coefficient rings. Since $p_2\Delta=1_P$, it gives $Rp_{2*}R\Delta_*\simeq R(1_P)_*=1$. Here $R\Delta_*=\Delta_*$ by exactness from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. This is a natural identification for every unbounded $M$. Use its inverse to write $M\simeq Rp_{2*}\Delta_*M$, followed by $Rp_{2*}(a_M^{-1})$.

Base change for the final arrow. The cartesian square has $f=q$, $f'=p_2$, $g=q$, $g'=p_1$. Its canonical exchange map $\beta_M:q^*Rq_*M\to Rp_{2*}p_1^*M$ is the unit--pullback-comparison--counit composite of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. To apply the bounded rational theorem with its general ring-object constructibility convention, take any constant-model $M\in\Dbc(P,\Lambda)$. On every stratum its cohomology has a finite constant local model, hence is locally finitely presented over the coefficient ring object by the final inclusion of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. The same finite stratification therefore witnesses constructibility in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], with the same finite cohomological bounds. Consequently $M$ belongs to the bounded category of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational], and clause (3) makes its canonical $\beta_M$ an isomorphism. This uses only the inclusion from constant-model constructibility into ring-object constructibility. By [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] the constant-model $\Dbc$ objects are exactly the $\Dctf$ generators. The extension statement [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] therefore makes this same $\beta_M$ an isomorphism for every $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(P,\Lambda))$. The properness and closure-preservation hypotheses were checked in Steps 1--5. Invert $\beta$ as a natural isomorphism; its direction is $Rp_{2*}p_1^*\to q^*Rq_*$, as required by clause (2).

source.place: Well-definedness (2): proper base change on the localizing closure

proof.text: Finish the unit, including the twist. The rational class $\delta_\Lambda$ exists by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients], from the tower and trace of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace]. Tensor it with $1_{p_1^*M}$ and apply $Rp_{2*}$ to obtain the middle arrow in clause (2). To identify its target, apply the Tate-twist clause of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] to $p_2:W\to P$, with $d=1$ and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Both schemes have $\ell$ invertible by Step 4, and these are precisely the condensed coefficients specified there; the additional annihilation condition concerns only finite rings and is not needed here. This identifies $\Lambda_W(1)$ with $p_2^*\Lambda_P(1)$. Apply [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing] to $p_2$, $A=p_1^*M$ and $B=\Lambda_P(1)$, and shift by $[2]$, to get $Rp_{2*}(p_1^*M(1)[2])\simeq(Rp_{2*}p_1^*M)(1)[2]$. Then apply $\beta_M^{-1}(1)[2]$ from Step 9. This specifies the shift and twist implicit in the final base-change arrow. Combining with Steps 7 and 8 gives exactly $\eta_M:M\to q^*Rq_*M(1)[2]$ with the displayed order of arrows.

source.place: Well-definedness (2): tensoring the diagonal class and twisted proper base change

proof.text: Construct the counit. Set $A=\Lambda_P(1)[2]$ and $B=K$ in [det-thm-sf-pf-field-localizing] for the proper map $q$. Tensor symmetry and $q^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_P(1)[2]=q^*K(1)[2]$ rewrite the inverse projection isomorphism as $Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\simeq K\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rq_*\Lambda_P(1)[2]$. The trace of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-trace], extended to $\Lambda=E,\Qlb$ by [det-prop-diagonal-tower-coefficients], gives $1_K\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q$ into $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\Lambda_Y\simeq K$. Define $\varepsilon_K$ to be this composite. All these arrows lie in the full localizing subcategories checked in Step 5.

source.place: Well-definedness (3): the projection-formula and trace composite

proof.text: Naturality and exactness. Each unit constituent is natural in $M$: for $u:M\to M'$ the middle tensor square commutes because $(p_1^*u\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)=(1\otimes\delta_\Lambda)\circ(p_1^*u\otimes1)$ with the respective sources and targets. The other squares are naturality of the adjunction unit, the composition comparison, and the exchange transformation already used. Pasting gives $q^*Rq_*(u)(1)[2]\circ\eta_M=\eta_{M'}\circ u$. For $v:K\to K'$, bifunctoriality gives $(v\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q)=(1\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_q)\circ(v\otimes1)$, and naturality of the projection map gives $v\circ\varepsilon_K=\varepsilon_{K'}\circ Rq_*q^*(v)(1)[2]$. Exactness and shift compatibility of derived tensor and the canonical projection transformation are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; pullbacks and the proper pushforwards are exact by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] and [det-proper-image-localizing-proper]. Together with the exact shift functor $[2]$ on the derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], these facts make the source and target functors of $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ exact. The naturality equations just proved therefore give the asserted natural transformations of exact functors on the stated localizing categories. The names unit and counit specify candidate adjunction maps here; the triangle identities are the separate node det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-triangle and are not assumed in this construction.

source.place: Final sentence: natural transformations of exact functors

proof_origin.place: Well-definedness (1)--(3), expanded open--closed support argument and explicit functor domains
